correctness.rationale: The explicit linear isometry Θ:Z→ℓ∞((Z⊗πZ)**) follows from projective simple tensor norm equality, and its normalized coordinate sequences are isometric to the Lorentz basis. Allowed-exponent all-point estimates use the dual of the Hölder inclusion ℓ_{q′}→d(w,1) from [1, equation (3.8)]. For forbidden exponents the tensor fiber is an isometric hereditary-ℓ1 copy with no strongly normal sequences; restriction of the full predual to the fiber is an open surjection, and relative weak-star equals weak convergence. These verify (H1) and (H2) of [1, Theorem 3.1], which excludes every forbidden q for all normalized sequences in the fiber, including subsequences and blocks. Series comparison shows exact [r,∞), r>1, and empty sets. This is an analytic proof, not experimental extrapolation.

value.rationale: This addresses the two specific mathematically motivated cases left open in §8 of [1]. Spaceability asserts stability under all nonzero linear combinations inside an infinite-dimensional closed family and is not implied by a single sequence with the same spectrum. The projective tensor technique handles both logarithmically corrected endpoint inclusion and entirely empty exponent spectrum while preserving symmetry, weak nullity and all three selection spectra; no arbitrary unmotivated invariant is introduced.
